subject: chemistry
title: Formulations
key_idea: A formulation is a mixture designed as a useful product. Each chemical in it has a particular purpose. The components are mixed in carefully measured quantities, so the product always has the properties it needs.

blocks.text: This section covers what makes a mixture a formulation and where formulations are used.

items.meaning: A mixture designed as a useful product, made by mixing carefully measured quantities of its components.
One of the chemicals in a mixture.

items: Many products are complex mixtures in which each chemical has a **particular purpose**.
Fuels, cleaning agents, paints and medicines are formulations.
Alloys, fertilisers and foods are formulations too.
You do not need to know the names of the components in a branded product.
A formulation is a mixture designed for a purpose.
Each component does a particular job.

blocks.text: This section covers how a formulation differs from an ordinary mixture.

items: The components are mixed in **carefully measured quantities**.
This gives the product the properties it needs.
The composition is the same every time the product is made.
Crude oil is a mixture, but it is not a formulation: it is not designed for a purpose.

diagram.alt: Comparing an ordinary mixture such as crude oil with a formulation.

items: Measured amounts give the required properties.
A formulation is a mixture, but not every mixture is a formulation.

sections.heading: Percentage by mass of a component

blocks.text: This section covers how to find how much of a formulation is one component.

blocks.formula: percentage by mass = (mass of component ÷ total mass of the formulation) × 100
blocks.label: Percentage by mass
where: total mass of the formulation in grams (g)

items.text: Find the total mass of all the components.
Divide the mass of the component by the total mass.
Multiply by 100 to give a percentage.

blocks.text: For example, 30 g of one component in a 200 g sample is 30 ÷ 200 × 100 = 15%.

diagram.alt: Calculate the percentage by mass of a component, with new numbers each time.
diagram.question: A sample of a formulation has a mass of {total} g. It contains {part} g of one component. Calculate the percentage by mass of that component.
working: Percentage by mass = mass of component ÷ total mass × 100

items: Divide by the total mass of all the components.

checks.a: A mixture that has been designed as a useful product, made by mixing the components in carefully measured quantities.

checks.q: Give two reasons why crude oil is not a formulation.
checks.a: It is not a useful product (not designed for a specific purpose). It is not mixed in carefully measured quantities.

checks.q: A 200 g sample of a cleaning product contains 30 g of one component. Calculate the percentage by mass of that component.

exam_phrases: (crude oil is a mixture but) not a useful product
(crude oil is) not designed for a specific purpose
(and) not mixed in carefully measured quantities
not the same composition all the time

mistakes.wrong: Crude oil is not a formulation because it is not a mixture.
mistakes.right: Crude oil is a mixture, but it is not a useful product and not designed for a specific purpose.
A formulation is designed as a useful product and mixed in carefully measured quantities.

mistakes.wrong: Percentage of methanol = 23.3 ÷ 265.5 × 100, dividing by the mass of ethanol only.
mistakes.right: Divide by the total mass of every component: 23.3 ÷ (265.5 + 23.3 + 3.0 + 1.5) × 100 = 7.9%.

worked_example.question:
Crude oil is a mixture of many different compounds.

Give two reasons why crude oil is not a formulation.
answer_points: It is not a useful product (it is not designed for a specific purpose).
It is not mixed in carefully measured quantities (it is not the same composition all the time).
worked_example.tip: Each reason is a separate mark: not a useful product, and not mixed in carefully measured quantities.

exam_phrases: A formulation has a specific / consistent proportion of components
Formulation (the name for a mixture where substances are combined in exact amounts)

mistakes.wrong: A formulation is the same as any other mixture.
mistakes.right: A formulation has a specific, consistent proportion of components.

mistakes.wrong: The amounts of each component in a formulation can change from batch to batch.
mistakes.right: The proportions of the components are specific and consistent, so each batch is the same.

worked_example.question:
When a painkiller is sold to the public, it is sold as a formulation, not as a pure substance.

Explain how a formulation and a mixture are different.
answer_points: A formulation has a specific, consistent proportion of components.
worked_example.tip: One mark: the idea of fixed, exact proportions is what separates a formulation from a mixture.
